speaker: Doctor
text:
I need to understand the timeline of your symptoms: how long have you been experiencing confusion, abdominal pain, and vomiting, and did these symptoms start suddenly or gradually?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Electrolytes, Liver_Function_Tests, Amylase_Lipase.

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old female. The patient presents to the emergency department with confusion that started this morning. The patient's husband reports that she initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating and has vomited 3 times. The patient has progressively become more confused throughout the day. The patient's past medical history includes morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts.

speaker: Patient
text: sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; given your recent sleeve gastrectomy and history of depression, could your vomiting be food poisoning (fever, diarrhea) or alcohol-related, and have you noticed any black or tarry stools? REQUEST TEST: Iron_Ferritin, Vitamin_B12, Magnesium_Potassium, Toxicology_Screen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your blood work is normal despite the vomiting and confusion, have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), and have you recently consumed any unknown supplements or medications? REQUEST TEST: Coombs_Test, GGT, Bilirubin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Wernicke Encephalopathy (likely due to chronic alcohol use or thiamine deficiency post-bariatric surgery, presenting with confusion, vomiting, and abdominal pain).
